summary: Request to split token/quota accounting per ingress path to prevent webhook-heavy workflows triggering 429s
description:
Issue summary: Customer is seeing repeated 429s for normal webhook callback traffic that coincides with large background embed imports. They believe accounting is conflating tokens generated by webhook-delivered realtime requests with bulk embedding jobs because both ingress via the same API key and path.

Impact: Intermittent outages for time-sensitive webhook consumers (latency spikes up to 7s, followed by 429s) causing missed notifications and customer-side retries. Affects multiple teams inside SignalPlay during daily backfills.

Environment: prod/us-east with Dedicated pool attached (tenant: signalplay-dedicated).

Observed: 429 responses with X-RateLimit-* headers showing token exhaustion on tenant window. Console shows tenant token spend spikes aligned to scheduled embed pipelines. Customer expects webhook callbacks to be isolated from bulk ingest accounting.

Expected: Webhook callback traffic should be isolated (or able to be configured separately) so long-lived background embedding import does not cause realtime webhook throttles.
steps_to_reproduce:
1) Ingest bulk embeddings via the customer's scheduled backfill job (500k items over 20 minutes) using API key K-XXXXX bound to path /v1/embeddings/upload
2) At the same time, send webhook callback traffic through /v1/responses (same API key) at ~120rps
3) Observe 429 responses for /v1/responses after roughly 3-5 minutes with X-RateLimit-Remaining: 0
4) Stop the bulk job and observe quota refill and recovery for webhook path within 1-2 minutes
comments: 2026-03-12 10:02 - Aisha Kumar (SignalPlay): We've scheduled the backfill and noticed our webhook consumers (payments and delivery) started returning 429s. Can you confirm if there's a per-path option to separate accounting?

2026-03-12 10:20 - Support (Luca Reynolds): Thanks Aisha — filing this as a config/behavior question. Can you share the API key and timestamps for a sample event? We've requested logs from the rate-limiter team.
2026-03-12 11:05 - Aisha Kumar (SignalPlay): Provided sample request IDs and the K-XXXXX key in DM. Noted that switching to a different key for webhook traffic temporarily removed the 429s.

2026-03-12 13:30 - SRE (Marta Chen): Preliminary check: current tenant accounting is per-tenant and per-api-key windowed token buckets. Ingest and webhook calls count to the same refill window for the key unless route-level separation is configured.
investigation_notes: Checked rate-limiter metrics on prod (us-east) for tenant signalplay-dedicated: observed token window spike correlation with scheduled embed pipeline.
Confirmed console shows single token pool for the API key used by both ingestion and webhook paths.
Tested switching webhook consumers to a dedicated API key: immediate improvement and no 429s during simultaneous bulk ingest. Suggests accounting is key-centric by default.
Reviewed rate-limiter config: per-route quotas supported but not enabled for this tenant; default behavior is per-key and per-tenant aggregation.
Billing note: splitting keys may impact billing attribution and invoice line items — finance should be looped for enterprise customers before recommending permanent key split.
proposed_workarounds: Short term: Create a dedicated API key for realtime webhook traffic and pin low-latency priority class to that key (customer already validated improvement).
Medium term: Configure route-level quota separation for /v1/responses to isolate realtime credit consumption from bulk ingest endpoints.
Long term: Product consideration to expose 'ingress domain' accounting so customers can bind quota rules to ingress path patterns (e.g., /v1/embeddings/* vs /v1/responses/*).
resolution: Workaround applied: Support created a second API key for SignalPlay's webhook traffic and provided a short runbook for routing webhooks to the new key. Customer confirmed reduced 429s. Engineering/infra to evaluate feasibility of enabling per-route quota separation for dedicated tenants — tracking as product enhancement. Ticket remains open for follow-up until per-route option is scheduled.
